components.name: dti
components.method: 0.429·placement + 0.571·anchor (λ at n=4): placement of DeckCheck's score (of 96) within bracket 3; anchor = the mean of its twelve rubric grades (S 100, A 75, B 50, C 25, F 0); draw Normal(anchor, DTI_PRIOR_READ_SD = 4.0, a declared prior (one reading on this list)); an LLM's dated read of card quality, never ours

limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).

Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking; a win the goldfish cannot see (`alt_win_cards`) multiplies speed's weight by 0.5.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.

DeckCheck's Threat Index is a component at prior weight 0.15 (2026-10-19): one LLM's dated read of card quality, withheld when it describes another list; its interval is a declared prior sd of 4.0 on the anchor until three decks carry two readings on one list; its score places within the bracket, its twelve rubric grades anchor.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.

The weights are a Dirichlet prior (κ = 20.0) and the inputs are drawn from their posteriors: `score` is the median of 2000 seeded draws, `score_ci` its 90% interval, and every sd in `uncertainty` is declared, not estimated.
A placement within a group of n is a (n−1)-point scale and earns the share λ = (n−1)/(n−1+4) of its component, the rest going to the cited anchor; at n=3 that is one third.
A divergent `concordance` — the deck's instruments rank it far apart — prints the grade as a range, never a letter, and the judgment must address every outlier instrument.
rank over n=4 decks; no significance claim

open_questions.question: Do Silence, Snapback, March of Swirling Mist and the wheel-plus-removal cards get cast in real games, and do the swapped duals bring the commanders on time with no added ramp?

findings.note: validate-rating OK; rating --json re-run diff: components, withheld, code_score 67.2, score_point, bracket, limits, uncertainty, sensitivity all identical.

67 vs code_score 67.2: no gap claimed, so no double count. Plain-statement route for outliers is valid: the argument says the record does not explain mana/speed (better) vs dti/resilience (worse) and does not claim cancellation.

Figures match components: kill_by_turn_8 0.898, missed_land_drop_rate 0.1692, answer_cards 14, 2 classes, DTI 33. Ranks match concordance.instruments over n=4 (speed 1, mana 1, resilience 3, dti 4). The only logged game (001, 2026-10-06) predates v1.3.0 (sleeved 2026-10-19). All four outliers addressed.

context:numbers sentence 'No blockers and no removal: read board quality with care.' is verbatim and used as the goldfish-ceiling caveat, which is its meaning. Skeleton citations 0-3 are bare figure names that match the components.

Half of this question is already answered by artifacts: the context numbers give commander cast by T6 84%, mean first cast T5.308, colour on curve W88/U86/R84, and audit.consistency 0.896 (turn-3 land drops). 'Bring the commanders on time' is measured; only 'get cast in real games' (cards played) needs a rate. Split it or drop the on-time clause. The argument also calls it 'the pilot's own open question', but it is the rating's.

judgment.argument: What the measured components cannot see is play. No game is logged on this list, no survey, no Forge run on it, and the only game on record was played before the changes that gave the deck its answers, so it speaks to none of them. Four instruments disagree, and I answer each by name. Speed (kill_by_turn_8 0.898) ranks the deck first in bracket three, but the goldfish has no blockers or removal, so it is a ceiling and I will not lift the number for it. Mana (missed_land_drop_rate 0.1692) also ranks first; the record holds nothing unmeasured about the land pass beyond the pilot's own open question whether the swapped duals bring the commanders on time, so it stays as measured. DeckCheck's Threat Index (33) ranks the deck last and resilience (14 answer cards, two classes answered) ranks it third. Both are already scored in full, and the record has no game showing whether the new answers work, so nothing unmeasured moves either. The record does not explain why the clock and land drops read the deck first while DeckCheck reads it last. I do not claim the instruments cancel. My number therefore sits at code_score. It is no higher because nothing has been played on this list, and no lower because every weakness I can name is already a component.
